text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- Fears raised in Sweden that interest rates may rise following Finland's decision to link the markka to Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), but it will not influence the Swedish government's position on ERM.
- Leader of the opposition Centre party, Esko Aho, said the time was not yet ripe for Finland to join ERM.
- Almost three-quarters of Finns of all age groups and, across the political spectrum are against tax cuts if they erode social security, an opinion poll shows.
- For the ruling Social Democrats, this weekend's European Parliament elections will be a test of Finns' support for joining the ERM. Many Finns seen unprepared for rush towards EMU.
- Director of Finnish Immigration Institute says Finland should follow Swedish example and create a post for an anti-discrimination advocate.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Economists and economic decision-makers welcome ERM link level as a small, pleasant surprise.

- Big Finnish forestry companies due to report eight-month results this week -- news is expected to point the way for the Helsinki bourse in the coming months, says Merita Pankkiiriliike managing director Reijo Knuutinen.
- Helsinki Stock Exchange chief Juhani Erma criticises proposed rules regulating companies' buy-back of their shares -- says rules too complicated and too stiff.
- UPM-Kymmene said to be interested in buying Canadian Repap Enterprises paper mill in New Brunswick.
- Neste Chemicals says it will launch a biodegradable plastic in 1998.
- Share lending has foothold among Finland's professional investors via SOM's Lex system.
DEMARI
- Citizens' faith in the government's ability to reduce unemployment has markedly declined during the year, shows a poll conducted by the SAK Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions.
AAMULEHTI
- Opposition Centre party leader Esko Aho called for parliament to end its election recess to debate the ERM link. Prime Minister Lipponen rejects call.
- ERM linkage grist for the mill of Finnish anti-EU groups.
